records.excerpt: "agrosphere-estate-service/docs/MILESTONE_1A_REPORT.md:38: Domain writes and mandatory outbox inserts share one JPA-managed database transaction. The dispatcher locks due rows with SKIP LOCKED and sends persistent mandatory messages to durable agrosphere.domain using publisher confirms. Returns, nacks and exceptions retry with configurable exponential backoff; exhausted events remain FAILED for operator-controlled replay. Publication defaults disabled while preserving outbox records. Confirmation/crash ambiguity permits duplicates with the same eventId. Consumers must deduplicate consumer_name/eventId transactionally, ACK after commit and reject stale revisions. No exactly-once delivery is claimed. The implementation follows the [Spring AMQP confirm/return API](https://docs.spring.io/spring-amqp/reference/amqp/template.html)."

records.head: e2a080f8c83339f20a3cb3e26506859da100c402
records.excerpt: "excerpt": "Consumer transaction: insert (consumer_name,event_id) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; apply projection only when inserted, in the same transaction; commit before ACK. Publisher writes outbox with domain mutation; relay publishes persistent messages with confirms and marks published only after confirmation. Duplicates are expected. Bounded retries and DLQ handling are required before consumers ship. Estate Service implements its v2 relay in Milestone 1A; consumer handlers remain separate work. Validate forecast period ordering and business semantics in applications as JSON Schema cannot enforce them.",

records.excerpt: "excerpt": "Estate OpenAPI now defines sixteen business operations and Problem Details, JWT scope, pagination and optimistic versions. V1 EstateCreated requires companyId, which M1A does not own; v2 avoids inventing that identity. V1 block update fields cannot express status/count changes. Estate Service publishes only v2; existing v1 consumers must explicitly migrate to agrosphere.<EventType>.v2. There is no dual publishing.",

records.excerpt: "excerpt": "Only canonical IDs, estate/parent IDs, lifecycle status and snapshot revision are retained. M1A emits no division events, so division membership is inferred from validated block snapshots and explicitly marked inferred; independent division lifecycle cannot be established yet. Estate/block lifecycle is authoritative; revisions handle update-before-create and stale delivery. An estate or block inactivation blocks future writes but does not erase spatial history. Membership/lifecycle changes can require operator reconciliation of existing geometry.",
records.reason: Orchestrator reports and nested test fixtures are not manifest-bound application repository evidence.

records.excerpt: "excerpt": "Preparation found these differences: foundation pom/ADR-0005 use Java 25, while the explicit request asks for Java 21; Spatial targets 21 and was fully verified on 21. ADR-0008 says Java21 although the working Estate pom/README actually use Java25; Estate was left unchanged. M1A is available and publishes v2, so Spatial consumes existing v2 contracts rather than incompatible foundation v1 events. M1A emits no division lifecycle events: division membership is inferred from block snapshots and marked inferred, with authoritative division lifecycle deferred to a coordinated future release. Infrastructure already provisions the service-owned PostGIS database; no central infrastructure changes were needed. ADR-0009 and MILESTONE_1B.md record these decisions.",

records.excerpt: "excerpt": "Preparation found these differences: foundation pom/ADR-0005 use Java 25, while the explicit request asks for Java 21; Spatial targets 21 and was fully verified on 21. ADR-0008 says Java21 although the working Estate pom/README actually use Java25; Estate was left unchanged. M1A is available and publishes v2, so Spatial consumes existing v2 contracts rather than incompatible foundation v1 events. M1A emits no division lifecycle events: division membership is inferred from block snapshots and marked inferred, with authoritative division lifecycle deferred to a coordinated future release. Infrastructure already provisions the service-owned PostGIS database; no central infrastructure changes were needed. ADR-0009 and MILESTONE_1B.md record these decisions.",

records.head: ab6289d42dcc0ba4a956c39ed55b34c2f0c49746
records.excerpt: Implement AgroSphere Milestone 1B Spatial Service and estate identity projection only. Read affected AGENTS.md files, architecture ADR-0008, the completed Estate Service report, infrastructure configuration and contracts 0.2.0 first. Preserve independent Git roots and service-owned databases. Consume the Estate Service v2 snapshots with transactional consumer_name/eventId deduplication, revision-aware updates, retry/DLQ/replay and reconciliation. Implement spatial-owned PostGIS geometry and RFC 7946 WGS84 API contracts, using canonical estate/block UUIDs without cross-database access. Reject new operational use of inactive blocks and label synthetic fixtures SIMULATED. Add contract/security/PostGIS integration and duplicate/out-of-order event tests. Validate builds, migrations, permissions and Docker, document actual results and blockers, and stop after Milestone 1B. Do not add operations, telemetry, AI, web/immersive functionality or deploy to Azure.
